title: The constructed Int is a discretely ordered ring generated by 1, with unique maps out
statement: The constructed `Int` has no elements beyond its two constructors (every element is +/- a natural number), is generated by 0 under +1 and -1 (an induction principle), is discretely ordered at EVERY point (nothing strictly between a and a+1), is totally ordered, is non-trivial (0 != 1), and any two maps out of it that agree at 0 and satisfy the same +1 and -1 recurrences are equal. These are the properties that separate the integers from the rationals (which fail discreteness) and from lexicographic Z[x] (which is discretely ordered but is not generated by 1).

formal.statement: theorem Int.Characterization.induction : ((x0 : ((x0 : Int) -> Prop)) -> ((x1 : x0 Int.zero) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : Int) -> ((x3 : x0 x2) -> x0 (Int.add x2 Int.one)))) -> ((x3 : ((x3 : Int) -> ((x4 : x0 x3) -> x0 (Int.add x3 (Int.neg Int.one))))) -> ((x4 : Int) -> x0 x4)))))

evidence.supports: Int is generated by 0 under +1 and -1: the property lexicographic Z[x] fails.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example characterization_status 2>/dev/null) && test "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Ec '^int-generation[[:space:]]+Int[.]Characterization[.]induction[[:space:]]+\[\][[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: Both steps are definitional in the normalized ofNat/negSucc representation -- `ofNat n + 1` iota-reduces to `ofNat (succ n)`, `0 + (-1)` to `negSucc 0`, and `negSucc n + (-1)` to `negSucc (succ n)` -- so each branch is `Nat.rec` applied to the hypotheses with no rewriting. Two `Weakening` variants replace the +1 and the -1 step with `True`; the kernel refuses this declaration in both cases.

evidence.supports: No junk: every integer is + or - a natural number.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example characterization_status 2>/dev/null) && test "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Ec '^int-no-junk[[:space:]]+Int[.]Characterization[.]of_nat_or_neg[[:space:]]+\[\][[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: Together with `Int.Characterization.cases` (exhaustive constructor case analysis, admitted in the same package) this says the carrier has exactly the elements the construction puts in it.

evidence.supports: Discreteness at every point: nothing strictly between a and a+1. This is the property the rationals fail.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example characterization_status 2>/dev/null) && test "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Ec '^int-order[[:space:]]+Int[.]Characterization[.]discrete_everywhere[[:space:]]+\[\][[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: Derived, not assumed: the interval (a, a+1) is translated down to (0, 1) through -a with `add_lt_add_of_le_of_lt` and `le_refl`, and the endpoints normalise to 0 and 1 by the ring laws, landing in the prelude's `no_int_between`. The 0/1 instance alone would leave the general statement to a reader's translation-invariance argument; this is the machine-checked one.

evidence.supports: The UNIQUENESS half of the universal property: two maps out of Int agreeing at 0 with the same +/-1 recurrences are equal. Paired with the existence half (F:int-categoricity) this makes Int the initial Z-structure.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example characterization_status 2>/dev/null) && test "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Ec '^int-universal-property[[:space:]]+Int[.]Characterization[.]rec_unique[[:space:]]+\[\][[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: Proved from `Int.Characterization.induction`. `characterization_tests::the_int_hypothesis_shapes_are_satisfiable` instantiates the whole premise list and admits the result, so the theorem is not vacuous. Since 2026-08-18 it is also what proves the Int-side half of `Int.Characterization.iso`: `psi . iter` and the identity map agree at 0 with the same recurrences, so they are equal.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the integer prelude's whole trusted surface is empty.

provenance.source: hand-built foundational library; the property list is the standard characterization of the integers among ordered rings, authored here

notes:
WHAT THIS FACT CLAIMS AND WHAT F:int-categoricity ADDS. These properties are proved to HOLD of `Int`. Until 2026-08-18 it was NOT proved that they determine `Int` up to isomorphism -- the existence half of the universal property, a map `Int -> R` built from an arbitrary target's own data, was missing, so `rec_unique` was uniqueness of a map nobody had constructed. That half is now built (`Int.Characterization.iter` with `iter_zero`/`iter_succ`/`iter_pred`) and the categoricity theorem that follows from it is F:int-categoricity, which supersedes this fact's former caveat. The categoricity there is over Z-STRUCTURES (a point with an automorphism), not over discretely ordered rings: the order properties recorded HERE are what separate Z from Q and from lexicographic Z[x], and they are proved of `Int` rather than assumed of an arbitrary target. Ordered-ring laws alone pin nothing (the rationals satisfy every one of them), which is why the no-junk, generation and discreteness rows are the substance here and the ordered-ring rows are not restated as this fact's evidence.

2026-08-30: marked as restating [[F:int-characterization-induction]], because this fact's `formal.statement` IS `Int.Characterization.induction` verbatim -- the same proposition the narrower fact states.

SEPARATE FINDING, NOT REPAIRED HERE, NEEDS A DECISION. This fact's TITLE claims "a discretely ordered ring generated by 1, with unique maps out" and its evidence cites FOUR declarations (`induction`, `of_nat_or_neg`, `discrete_everywhere`, `rec_unique`), while its `formal.statement` carries only the first. So the prose claims a four-part characterization and the formal side delivers one conjunct. Nothing detects that today: the statement pin checks that each field does not CHANGE, never that the two AGREE, and the axiom footprint is blind to it. Repairing it means amending a pinned statement to a conjunction that does not yet exist as one kernel theorem, which is a real decision rather than an edit.
